thread:
Maya R: Heads-up — need a lightweight bench for Sentinel-9b-v1 onboarding. Looking for p95 tail, steady-state tokens/s, mem (GPU), and cost-estimate. Can someone run a short 1k-token sweep on a g5x2 (2xA10G) and post raw profiler traces? Use the perf-harness with --seq-lens 8,64,256. ETA EOD? Thanks.

Evan: I can take this. Which model repo tag are we using? v1.0 or the fused-kernel build?

Maya R: v1.0 for smoke. If that passes we'll test fused-kernel later. Also prefer batch sizes 1/4/8. Please include kv-cache warmup time.

Priya: I have a free slot on g5x2 in us-west-2 at 3pm PT, can run. Will use the standard eval set (smoke-1k-samples). Any special tokenization flags?

Maya R: default tokenizer, but set max_new_tokens=512. Add --trace-kernel on the harness.

Evan: running now. Command I used:
```
perf-harness run --model=sentinel-9b-v1 --device=gpu --gpus=2 --batch-sizes=1,4,8 --seq-lens=8,64,256 --max-new-tokens=512 --trace-kernel --output=json
```

bench-bot: smoke run complete — status: SUCCESS. Summary: p50=45ms p95=210ms tokens/s (steady)=3200 mem=11.9GB per-GPU. Full artifact: https://artifacts.redwood/sentinel9b/smoke/1773879001

Sam: quick note — p95 210ms at batch1 seems high vs. our sim target 180ms. Can we check kernel selection? Maybe fallback to non-fused path on A10 profiles.

Priya: uploaded profiler trace to the artifact. Key hotspot is attention_forward CUDA kernel at step ~60. Will re-run with TORCH_NVFUSER=0 to compare.

Evan: re-ran with nvfuser=0, p95 -> 190ms, tokens/s -> 3050. Looks like nvfuser build regressed here. Opening a perf issue.

Maya R: thanks. Action items: (1) Evan files perf issue linking artifacts, (2) Priya to re-run on fused-kernel build tomorrow, (3) publish smoke summary to model-onboarding/docs and tag release. :thumbsup:

Evan: filed https://issues.redwood/inf/9876 - added logs and perf traces. Assigned to runtime team.

Priya: will run fused-kernel tomorrow morning and ping this thread with results. :eyes: 

Maya R: awesome — closing for now, keep updates in thread.
